close_reason: Done in 2baf002. Added a 'Do not simplify the four-test structure' section to the module docstring of tests/log_redaction.rs naming workspace AGENTS.md Security-testing Pattern 2 and the failure mode of removing each test. Defense against the 'delete the scaffolding' refactor.
description:
tests/log_redaction.rs has FOUR test functions where a naive reader sees only one as the 'real' test:

1. log_capture_captures_traced_output — harness self-test (proves the capture mechanism works)
2. log_capture_detects_a_leak_when_one_exists — negative control with a deliberately-leaky type
3. auth_token_never_appears_in_tracing_capture — the actual BearerAuth canary
4. basic_auth_credentials_never_appear_in_tracing_capture — the actual BasicAuth canary

A contributor reviewing this file may suggest 'tests #1 and #2 are scaffolding — delete them, keep only #3 and #4.' This is the wrong simplification.

Defense: without #1, a future regression in LogCapture (subscriber install fails, MakeWriter misroutes) silently makes #3 and #4 pass vacuously — no log output means the canary needle is not found means the assertion passes. Without #2, a regression in the negative-assertion plumbing (e.g. a future refactor that filters output before contents() returns it) silently makes #3 and #4 pass without actually defending anything.

#3 and #4 internally also assert that ['constructed auth provider'] and ['[REDACTED]'] appear in the capture (lines 105-106 and 127-128), providing per-test proof-of-capture. This is correct paranoia.

The pattern (harness self-test + negative control + per-test proof-of-capture + the negative-assertion canary) is the workspace AGENTS.md 'Security testing' pattern #2 executed correctly. Do not simplify it.
title: Log-capture canary harness with negative control: defend against 'just delete the self-tests'
